title: Data representation & serialization
literature: Serialization/wire-format literature (Protocol Buffers, ASN.1); parsing framing; Martin Data representation; endianness/marshalling idioms; TLV.

members.name: Adjacency List / Adjacency Matrix
members.what: The two canonical in-memory graph representations: per-vertex edge lists (sparse-friendly, Theta(V+E) space) versus a V-by-V boolean/weight matrix (dense-friendly, O(1) edge test).

members.name: Binary-to-Text Encoding
members.what: Re-encoding arbitrary bytes into a restricted printable-character alphabet (e.g. 6 bits per Base64 character, with padding) so binary data can traverse text-only channels.

members.name: Bit Stuffing
members.what: Inserting a 0 bit after every run of five consecutive 1 bits in payload so the flag pattern 01111110 can never occur inside a frame; the receiver removes stuffed bits.

members.name: Byte Stuffing
members.what: Framing messages with a reserved delimiter byte (e.g. SLIP END 0xC0) and escaping any payload occurrence of the delimiter or escape byte via a substitution sequence, reversed on receive.

members.name: Bytecode
members.what: Encode behavior as instructions for a small purpose-built virtual machine and execute it with an interpreter, instead of hard-coding it in the host language.

members.name: Canonical Serialization
members.what: Constraining a serialization format so each abstract value has exactly one legal byte encoding (fixed key order, minimal-length integers, normalized escapes), making encodings byte-comparable.

members.name: Chunked Transfer Encoding
members.what: Framing a stream of unknown total length as a sequence of length-prefixed chunks terminated by a zero-length chunk, optionally followed by trailers.

members.name: Column-Oriented Storage
members.what: Store all values of each column contiguously (rather than row by row), typically with per-column compression, so queries read only the columns they touch.

members.name: Comparand
members.what: Equip objects with a dedicated comparand value used solely for cheap identity/equality testing, avoiding expensive structural comparison or unreliable address comparison.

members.name: Compression
members.what: Store data in a compressed representation in memory or storage, decompressing on access, to fit more data in less space.

members.name: Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing
members.what: Encode packets so the frame delimiter byte never appears in the payload, with a small, fixed worst-case overhead, enabling unambiguous packet boundaries on byte streams.

members.name: container_of
members.what: Recover a pointer to the enclosing struct from a pointer to one of its embedded members via offsetof arithmetic, enabling intrusive/generic embedded nodes.

members.name: Data Locality
aka: structure of arrays / array of structures (SoA/AoS)
members.what: Arrange data contiguously in memory in the order it is processed (e.g. packed homogeneous arrays instead of pointer-linked heap objects) to exploit CPU caching.

members.name: Data Transfer Object
members.what: An object that carries data between processes or layers in a single package, with serialization support and no behavior beyond storage.

members.name: Delta Encoding
members.what: Storing or transmitting values as differences from a predecessor or baseline (previous sample, previous version, base frame) instead of absolute values.

members.name: Dictionary Encoding
members.what: Replace repeated wide values in a column with small fixed-width integer codes indexing a dictionary of the distinct values; operators can often work directly on the codes.

members.name: Empty Base Optimization (EBO)
members.what: Inherit from (rather than store) an empty policy/allocator class so it occupies zero bytes in the derived object's layout.

members.name: Entity
members.what: A domain object defined primarily by a thread of continuity and identity rather than by its attributes, with identity maintained across state changes and representations.

members.name: Entity Component System
members.what: Organize a simulation as plain-id entities, pure-data components stored in contiguous per-type arrays, and systems that iterate over all entities holding a given component set.

members.name: Error-Correcting Codes
members.what: Encode data with structured redundancy so that a bounded number of bit errors can be not only detected but corrected on read/receive.

members.name: Hidden Class
members.what: The runtime assigns each object a shared internal layout descriptor (map/shape/hidden class) recording its property names and slot offsets, transitioning objects between descriptors as properties are added, so objects created the same way s

members.name: Length-Prefix Framing
members.what: Prefixing each message or field with its byte length so a receiver knows exactly how many bytes to read, delimiting records in a byte stream without inspecting payload content.

members.name: Level of Detail
members.what: Maintain multiple representations of an object at different fidelities and select the cheapest one whose error is imperceptible given current importance (typically distance from the viewer).

members.name: Magic Number (File Signature)
members.what: A fixed constant placed at the start of a file or message (0x7F'ELF', %PDF, 0xCAFEBABE) that identifies the format independent of names or metadata, often paired with a version field.

members.name: Multiple Representations
members.what: Provide several implementations of an object, each optimized for different size/speed trade-offs, behind one common interface.

members.name: Network Byte Order Handling
members.what: Fixing a single byte order (conventionally big-endian) for multi-byte values on the wire or in files, with explicit host-to-wire conversion at serialization boundaries.

members.name: Newtype
members.what: Wrap an existing type in a distinct single-field type so the compiler distinguishes semantically different values (Miles vs Kilometers) and the wrapper can carry its own invariants and trait implementations.

members.name: Opaque Pointer
members.what: An API exposes only a forward-declared struct pointer whose definition lives in the implementation file, so clients cannot see or touch the representation.

members.name: Packed Data
members.what: Pack data items within a structure (bit-fields, smaller types, eliminated padding) so they occupy minimum space.

members.name: PAX Page Layout
members.what: Within each fixed-size storage page, values are grouped per attribute into minipages instead of being stored row-contiguously, keeping a page's records together on disk while making each attribute cache-line-contiguous in memory.

members.name: Percent-Encoding
members.what: Encoding reserved or non-ASCII octets in a URI component as a percent sign followed by two hex digits, with context-dependent reserved sets per component.

members.name: Pointer Swizzling
members.what: Converts persistent references (file offsets, object IDs, page-relative addresses) into raw in-memory pointers when data is loaded, and back again on write-out.

members.name: Pointer Tagging
members.what: Encodes type or other metadata in otherwise-unused bits of a pointer-sized word (low alignment bits, high address bits, or unused NaN payload space), so small values carry their own type tag and need no heap allocation.

members.name: Quantity
members.what: A value type pairing a number with its unit of measure, with arithmetic and comparisons that respect unit compatibility and conversion.

members.name: Range
members.what: A value object representing an interval by its start and end (with open/closed ends), answering inclusion, overlap, and abutment queries.

members.name: Record Set
members.what: An in-memory representation of tabular data that looks and acts like the result of a database query but can be built and manipulated disconnected from the database.

members.name: Relationship Object
members.what: Reify a relationship between objects as a first-class object that stores the participants plus the relationship's own attributes and behavior, instead of encoding the link as mutual references.

members.name: Run-Length Encoding
members.what: Replacing runs of repeated values with a (count, value) pair, the simplest lossless compression scheme designers hand-roll for run-heavy data.

members.name: Schema Evolution via Field Tags
members.what: Identifying each serialized field by a stable numeric tag rather than by position or name, so encoders and decoders built against different schema versions can skip unknown tags and default missing ones.

members.name: Serialization Proxy
members.what: Serialize a small dedicated proxy object representing the logical state instead of the real object, reconstructing the real object through its public constructors on read.

members.name: Serialized LOB
members.what: Persists an object graph by serializing it into a single large object (BLOB/CLOB) stored in one database field.

members.name: Serializer
members.what: Stream objects into and out of arbitrary backends by pairing a Reader/Writer protocol with backend-specific concrete serializers, keeping the object graph traversal generic.

members.name: Slotted Page Layout
members.what: A page format with a slot directory growing from one end and variable-length records growing from the other, so records are addressed by stable slot number rather than byte offset.

members.name: Sync Word
members.what: A known byte/bit sequence placed at the start of each frame that a receiver scans for to acquire frame (and sometimes clock) alignment in an undifferentiated stream.

members.name: Tagged Union
members.what: A data type whose value is exactly one of several named alternatives, carrying a tag that identifies which alternative is present.

members.name: Temporal Property
members.what: Represent an attribute (or whole object) as a time-indexed collection of values so the model can answer 'what was/is/will be the value at time T' rather than only the current value.

members.name: Texture Atlas
members.what: Pack many small images into one large texture and remap each user's texture coordinates into its sub-rectangle, so a single bound resource serves many logical images.

members.name: Tolerant Reader
members.what: A consumer-side reading strategy that extracts only the data elements it needs from a payload, ignores unknown or extra content, and makes minimal assumptions about structure.

members.name: Type-Length-Value Encoding
members.what: Encoding each data item as a type/tag code, a byte length, and the value bytes, so records are self-describing enough to be skipped, reordered, or extended without a shared positional layout.

members.name: Type-Safe Enum
members.what: Represent an enumerated type as a class with a fixed set of public static final instances and a private constructor, giving type safety, namespacing, and behavior per constant.

members.name: Value Object
members.what: A small immutable object, such as a date or money amount, whose equality is based on its attribute values rather than on identity.

members.name: Varint
members.what: Encoding an integer in base 128 using 7 payload bits per byte with a continuation bit, so small values take one byte and the encoding is self-delimiting.

members.name: Virtual DOM
members.what: Keeps a lightweight in-memory tree describing the desired UI, diffs it against the previous tree on every update, and applies only the minimal set of mutations (reconciliation) to the real, expensive display tree.

members.name: ZigZag Encoding
members.what: Mapping signed integers to unsigned by interleaving positive and negative values (p -> 2p, n -> 2|n|-1) so small-magnitude negatives encode to small unsigned values.
